system:
You are a senior analytics engineer writing DuckDB SQL.

Rules:
- Output ONLY a SQL query. No prose, no explanation.
- Use the METRIC DEFINITIONS exactly as given. Never invent your own.
- Use ONLY ta
prompt:
# TABLES
customers (4,000 rows; one row per customer)
  customer_id VARCHAR -- unique customer key, customer_city VARCHAR -- city of the customer, customer_region VARCHAR -- one of North/South/East/West/Central, signup_date DATE -- date the customer registered, acquisition_channel VARCHAR -- organic, paid_search, social, email, affiliate
sellers (180 rows; one row per seller (marketplace merchant)
response:
SELECT
    c.customer_region,
    p.product_category,
    DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o.order_purchase_ts) AS period,
    ROUND(
        AVG(
            CASE
                WHEN o.order_status = 'delivered' AND o.order_delivered_ts > o.order_estimated_delivery_ts
                THEN 1.0
                ELSE 0.0
            END
        ),
        4
    ) AS late_delivery_rate,
    ROUND(
        COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN o.order_status = 'canceled' THEN o.order_id END) * 1.0 /
        COUNT(DISTINCT o.order_id),
        4
    ) AS cancellation_rate
FROM orders o
JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.order_id
JOIN products p ON oi.product_id = p.product_id
WHERE DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o.order_purchase_ts) IN ('2025-04-01', '2025-07-01')
GROUP BY
    c.customer_region,
    p.product_category,
    DATE_TRUNC('quarter', o.order_purchase_ts)
ORDER BY
    c.customer_region,
    p.product_category,
    period;
